objective: Continuously improve Sortie-dogs on SWE-bench Lite dev23 while preserving usability in actual OpenCode CLI development sessions. Optimize autonomy, efficiency and visibility, not benchmark score alone.
instructions: Canonical source is main. At each improvement cycle follow the current main through the existing branch -> PR/confirmation -> main route. Preserve active branches and user changes. Use short-lived bench/swebench-dev23 branches/worktrees; do not develop long-lived parallel changes to plugin/runtime hotspots.

Reuse docs/swebench-lite-benchmark.md and the existing manifest generator, candidate preflight, supervisor and official grader. Start by reading retained dev23 results and their official reports, not by re-running finished or interrupted inference. Choose one failing case and one improvement theme; diagnose its real V2 history, fix, run targeted tests, and compare that one case before another full 23-case evaluation. A valid Sortie Coordinator self-execution route may successfully solve a case; do not force Worker delegation or rerun a correct task solely for a preferred route. Actual executor/model differences qualify performance comparisons, not task success. Preserve the immutable original requirements of already-running practical tasks.

After integration into main, freeze the candidate commit, package .tgz and SHA-256, runtime marker, manifest SHA-256, runner commit/scripts and all conditions. Run 23 distinct dev cases, pass@1, zero inference retries. Defaults for the established comparison: 8 inference slots, $2 per case, $46 reserved per full evaluation, official-image-testbed, 2400-second hard maximum. The native runner's 20-minute progress checkpoint, recent 5-minute activity extension and 3-minute read-stall policy remain in effect. Never describe each case as a fixed 40-minute run. Use the exact native launch command without tee or redirection.

Observe a real dog-worker-v010 session and its actual openai/gpt-6-luna-fast#max model in the exact candidate environment before widening the campaign. Reuse matching actual observations. Setup preflight, configured agents, zero-request provider failures and detached starts are not completed tasks or scores.

Each candidate also needs actual CLI usability evidence: use scripts/mission-cli-probe.mjs probe with mode=complete, the same frozen tgz, and a concrete original code-development task on a real repository/base commit (for example the selected failing public case). Preserve the original task, source changes, native validation command/exit/log, actual Worker model, completed Mission and succeeded acceptance receipt. A seed-file fixture, READY response, route-only probe or passing unit suite is not this check. Reserve this operation before starting; use a $2 maximum unless the remaining approved campaign budget warrants a documented different allocation.

Reserve each full evaluation, single-case attempt and practical CLI check through autodev-runner reserve before launch; register the absolute supervisor-state.json or observation.json path. All are inside the same $600 cumulative campaign (original $300 plus owner-authorized $300 added on 2026-10-11), including failed attempts and unknown-usage holds. Never reset accounting, reuse an attempt as a new run, or change a running candidate. Keep OpenCode implementation/supervision usage inside the same accounting. Admission limits are conservative estimates, not a guarantee about delayed usage or subscription dollars.

Score the immutable 23 predictions with the official harness, split=dev, one scoring worker. Patch presence, model narratives, fixture tests and supplementary diagnostics are not official resolution. Separate evaluator/environment failures and the official image ceiling from runtime/model failures. Preserve official resolved IDs and real-session results separately; a candidate is successful only when both the intended official comparison and actual practical task evidence are present.

For a completed main candidate, write a cycle receipt containing package/package_sha256, manifest/manifest_sha256, predictions/predictions_sha256, source_repo/commit/main_commit/main_integrated, runtime_marker, runner_root/runner_commit/runner_sha256 for the runner, supervisor, grader, model-cost and release-cli scripts, supervisor/scoring paths and practical {observation, task, repo, base_commit, verification:[{command,exit,log,log_sha256}]}. task is the immutable original prompt file and must match the CLI observation's task_sha256 and actual repository/base commit. Use the existing public row lock for the canonical dev23 set and keep official scoring split=dev, max_workers=1, retry_count=0. Run this runner's verify-cycle before claiming the cycle verified. Keep receipts, package, raw logs, predictions and datasets outside Git. Do not publish npm, tag/release, or globally replace the active host as a side effect of this development campaign.

Improve one actual usability bottleneck at a time. Do not add permissions, rejection gates, diagnostic layers or repeated reviews to make the score look safer. Reuse unchanged setup and successful evidence. Report the actual useful outcome, official resolved count/IDs, practical task result, cumulative API-equivalent priced/held exposure, blocker and next action. If score improves but real CLI work regresses, fix usability before expanding the next evaluation.
